title: The Tool Decathlon: Benchmarking Language Agents for Diverse, Realistic, and Long-Horizon Task Execution
authors_zh: Junlong Li, Wenshuo Zhao, Jian Zhao, Weihao Zeng, Haoze Wu, Xiaochen Wang, Rui Ge, Yuxuan Cao, Yuzhen Huang, Wei Liu, Junteng Liu, Zhaochen Su, Yiyang Guo, Fan Zhou, Lueyang Zhang, Juan Michelini, Xingyao Wang, Xiang Yue, Shuyan Zhou, Graham Neubig, Junxian He
paper_type_zh: 长程工具智能体基准、环境与评测轨迹发布
best_for_zh: 研究环境智能体轨迹、MCP 工具调用、终态 verifier、基准漂移与污染审计的读者
one_line: Toolathlon pairs 108 fuzzy cross-application tasks with initialized software states, recorded tool-use episodes, and deterministic terminal evaluators; its gated Verified trajectories are explicitly evaluation/audit-only and must not be used for training.
Toolathlon 将 108 个模糊的跨应用长程任务、初始化软件状态、工具调用 episode 与确定性终态 evaluator 绑定；其 gated Toolathlon-Verified 轨迹仅允许评测与审计，不得用于训练。
why: It makes the entire agent-data contract inspectable--task, tools, observations, environment mutation, terminal state check, run statistics, and failures--while illustrating why environment/evaluator version drift and contamination policy can dominate whether trajectory data is reproducible or reusable.
inclusion_reason: Toolathlon exposes a concrete long-horizon agent data boundary: fuzzy user tasks and initialized software state produce state-action-tool trajectories, while task-specific deterministic scripts attach terminal success to the resulting environment. Its later full-run trajectory archives and explicit anti-training policy make it useful for evaluation and failure auditing, but not a reusable post-training corpus.

title: Problem
问题
html:
The paper was first posted to arXiv in 2025, revised as arXiv v2 on 2026-02-26, and published at ICLR 2026. This dual date matters: toolathlon-2025 preserves the paper's first-release identity, while the venue field records the archival conference. The work asks how to evaluate language agents on realistic tasks that require many dependent tool calls, cross-application state changes, and recovery from noisy observations, rather than on a single API invocation or a static answer (Paper §§1–2; official ICLR and OpenReview records).

The benchmark contains 108 concise, deliberately fuzzy long-horizon tasks over 32 MCP-server/application surfaces, 604 MCP tools, and 7 local toolkits exposing 16 additional tools. A task exposes an average of 69.9 tools, with a range of 28–128; 72 of the 108 tasks have scripted state initialization and/or an initial workspace. The environments mix remote services with locally containerized applications such as Poste.io, Canvas, Kubernetes, and WooCommerce (Paper Table 2, p. 6; §§2.2–2.4).

The unit of analysis is not merely a prompt or final answer. A benchmark instance couples a fuzzy user instruction with task_config.json, a selected tool surface, optional preprocess or initial-workspace assets, task-specific ground truth, and an evaluation script. Running an agent produces an ordered user/assistant/tool history with tool calls, environment responses, execution status, timing, token and cost statistics, followed by a separate evaluator record. Thus the data object is an environment episode, while the correctness label is attached to the final state rather than to every state-action transition.

This distinction places the work in environment_agent_trajectory_data; the released episode preserves interaction with a mutable external substrate. It also belongs in benchmarks_evaluation_surfaces because each task defines an executable terminal scoring surface. It does not provide a post-training recipe, a step-level process-reward corpus, or evidence that the trajectories are licensed for training. The later gated Toolathlon-Verified release explicitly prohibits model-training use.

The Card is content-complete for bilingual L4 screening from the full paper and appendices plus official venue, project, code, and dataset artifacts. Its canonical metadata remains at the accepted L3_summary_ready level because raw gated archives, detailed decontamination files, general-purpose licenses, evaluator error rates, and an immutable cross-artifact replay manifest remain unavailable or unknown.

论文于 2025 年首次发布到 arXiv，2026-02-26 更新为 arXiv v2，并发表于 ICLR 2026。这个双重时间边界很重要：toolathlon-2025 保留论文首发年份，venue 字段则记录正式会议。该工作研究如何评测需要大量相互依赖的工具调用、跨应用状态修改以及从噪声观测中恢复的语言智能体，而不是只测试一次 API 调用或静态答案（论文第 1–2 节；ICLR 与 OpenReview 官方记录）。

该 benchmark 包含 108 个简洁且刻意保持模糊的长程任务，覆盖 32 个 MCP server/application 表面、604 个 MCP 工具，以及由 7 个本地 toolkit 提供的 16 个额外工具。每个任务平均暴露 69.9 个工具，范围为 28–128；108 个任务中有 72 个带脚本化状态初始化和/或 initial workspace。环境混合远程服务与本地容器化应用，包括 Poste.io、Canvas、Kubernetes 和 WooCommerce（论文表 2，第 6 页；第 2.2–2.4 节）。

分析单元不只是 prompt 或最终答案。一个 benchmark instance 将模糊用户指令与 task_config.json、选定工具面、可选 preprocess 或 initial-workspace 资产、任务专属 ground truth 和 evaluation script 绑定。智能体运行后产生有序的 user/assistant/tool 历史，其中包含工具调用、环境响应、执行状态、时间、token 与成本统计，随后另存 evaluator 记录。因此，数据对象是环境 episode，而正确性标签附着在终态，不附着在每个 state-action 转移上。

这一差别使其属于 environment_agent_trajectory_data：发布的 episode 保留了与可变外部 substrate 的交互。它也属于 benchmarks_evaluation_surfaces，因为每个任务都定义了可执行的终态评分面。该工作没有提供后训练 recipe、step-level process reward 语料，也没有证据表明轨迹获得训练复用许可；后续 gated Toolathlon-Verified 发布还明确禁止模型训练用途。

本卡依据完整论文与附录，以及官方 venue、project、code 和 dataset artifact，已具备用于双语 L4 筛选的内容深度。canonical metadata 仍保持已接受的 L3_summary_ready，因为原始 gated archive、详细 decontamination 文件、通用许可证、evaluator 错误率及跨 artifact 的不可变回放 manifest 仍不可获得或为 unknown。

title: Core idea
核心思路
html:
Toolathlon's central contribution is to bind realistic cross-application tasks, executable environment setup, full tool-interaction episodes, and a task-specific deterministic final-state evaluator into one benchmark contract. The paper models a task as a POMDP over state, action, observation, transition, reward, and instruction; its practical implementation narrows the reward to execution-based success after the agent has finished interacting (Paper §2.1, p. 3; §2.4, p. 5).

The task object contains a concise or fuzzy instruction, selected MCP servers and local tools, initialization assets, and static or dynamically retrieved ground truth. The trajectory object contains sequential assistant decisions, tool calls, tool responses, and evolving workspace/application state. In the checked current code, traj_log.json also records resolved configuration, request and session identifiers, timestamps, execution status, statistics, and costs; eval_res.json records pass plus details or a failure. These current filenames and fields describe repository commit 3b647e6, not a claim that every paper-era run used the identical serialization.

The feedback contract is deterministic terminal evaluation. Each task has a manually written evaluator that compares the resulting workspace or application state with a static snapshot or real-time ground truth. TaskEvaluator returns pass=true or false after a successful execution and pass=null when execution status is not SUCCESS. Agent-loop termination, a final natural-language answer, or claim_done is therefore not the terminal predicate for correctness; only the post-execution evaluator establishes benchmark success.

State-action detail and supervision granularity must not be conflated. The log preserves state-action-tool events, which makes state-action-level analysis possible, but the disclosed reward is one terminal binary outcome for the full episode. No per-step correctness label, critique, preference pair, dense reward, or process-reward trace is reported. The evaluator can observe the state fields its task-specific code queries; it cannot certify unqueried side effects, user satisfaction, semantic quality outside the predicate, or whether an alternative valid state was wrongly rejected.

The closest Atlas comparisons are MCP-AgentBench for MCP-centered agent evaluation, τ2-bench for stateful tool interaction, and TheAgentCompany for long-horizon work in a multi-application environment. Toolathlon's distinguishing contract is the combination of 108 fuzzy workflows, a broad MCP/local-tool surface, initialized cross-application state, and one deterministic end-state checker per task. The direction signal is not that programmatic checking is new, but that environment state and evaluator version must be treated as first-class parts of an agent-trajectory record.

Toolathlon 的核心贡献，是把真实跨应用任务、可执行环境初始化、完整工具交互 episode，以及任务专属的确定性终态 evaluator 绑定为一个 benchmark contract。论文把任务建模为包含 state、action、observation、transition、reward 与 instruction 的 POMDP；实际实现则把 reward 收窄为智能体完成交互后的 execution-based success（论文第 2.1 节，第 3 页；第 2.4 节，第 5 页）。

任务对象包含简洁或模糊指令、选定的 MCP server 与本地工具、初始化资产，以及静态或动态获取的 ground truth。轨迹对象包含连续的 assistant 决策、工具调用、工具响应与不断变化的 workspace/application state。在已检查的当前代码中，traj_log.json 还记录 resolved configuration、request/session ID、时间戳、执行状态、统计量和成本；eval_res.json 记录 pass 以及 detail 或 failure。这些当前文件名与字段对应仓库 commit 3b647e6，不能据此声称论文时期每次运行都使用完全相同的序列化格式。

反馈契约是确定性终态评测。每个任务都有人工编写的 evaluator，把最终 workspace 或 application state 与静态快照或实时 ground truth 比较。TaskEvaluator 在成功执行后返回 pass=true 或 false，执行状态不是 SUCCESS 时返回 pass=null。因此，agent loop 结束、最终自然语言回答或 claim_done 都不是正确性的 terminal predicate；只有执行后的 evaluator 才能确立 benchmark success。

不能混淆 state-action 细节与监督粒度。日志保留 state-action-tool 事件，因此可以进行 state-action-level 分析；但已披露 reward 只是完整 episode 的一个终态 binary outcome。论文没有报告逐步正确性标签、critique、preference pair、dense reward 或 process-reward trace。evaluator 能观察任务专属代码实际查询的状态字段；它不能认证未查询的副作用、用户满意度、谓词之外的语义质量，也不能保证其他有效终态不会被误拒。

Atlas 中最接近的对照包括侧重 MCP 智能体评测的 MCP-AgentBench、研究有状态工具交互的 τ2-bench，以及在多应用环境中研究长程工作的 TheAgentCompany。Toolathlon 的区别性契约，是把 108 个模糊 workflow、广泛的 MCP/本地工具面、初始化跨应用状态与逐任务确定性终态 checker 结合起来。其方向信号不是“程序化检查本身很新”，而是环境状态和 evaluator 版本必须成为智能体轨迹记录的一等组成部分。

title: Method
方法
html:
Inputs and task construction. Researchers and senior computer-science undergraduates first sourced needs freely from more than 50 candidate applications and then targeted important underrepresented applications. They converted those needs into concise, fuzzy tasks whose intended behavior must be inferred from the environment, examples, documents, or templates. After several weeks of checking, filtering, and refinement, the final pool contained 108 tasks. The paper reports 4–6 graduate-student hours to implement a task; 5–6 experienced authors then reviewed and revised each task for about five hours per task in each checking round, followed by benchmark-wide cross-checking and bug fixes (Paper §§3.1–3.2, pp. 5–7). Rejected counts, per-task source URLs, contributor identities, reviewer agreement, adjudication records, and an acceptance threshold are unknown.

Executable task bundle. A released task directory may include English or Chinese task and system-level instructions, task_config.json, preprocess scripts or an initial workspace, a ground-truth workspace/state, and evaluation/main.py. Configuration selects fewer than 10 relevant MCP servers for a task but loads every tool exposed by each selected server; configured local tools may include Python execution, web search, claim_done, sleep, overlong-output navigation, and context-history management. Across the paper snapshot there are 32 MCP-server/application surfaces, 604 MCP tools, and 16 local tools. 72 tasks have explicit state initialization (Paper Table 2, p. 6; §2.4; official repository tasks/finalpool/).

Interaction and generation. The evaluated model, not a teacher, generates the trajectory by alternating messages and tool calls with remote services and locally containerized software. Paper experiments use OpenAI Agents SDK v0.0.15, tool-error handling, truncation of tool outputs longer than 100K characters with 10K-character paging, and context-history management, with at most 100 turns per task (Paper §2.2 and Appendix B, pp. 14–15). The current repository additionally supports containerized and decoupled host loops and preliminary Claude Agent SDK integration; these later features must not be back-projected into the paper setup. The paper does not disclose one common temperature or normalized token/compute budget across providers.

Logging and outputs. At current repository commit 3b647e60713703d653584c23ff185e3b6cd67722, the primary episode log is traj_log.json, not JSONL. It stores resolved task config, request and session identifiers, initial and completion times, tool catalog/choice, execution status, message history with assistant tool_calls and tool responses, interaction/tool-call counts, token statistics, costs, resume metadata, and history path. The evaluator writes eval_res.json with pass=true/false/null plus details or failure; eval_stats.json aggregates run-level success and turn statistics. Exact paper-era field parity and raw archive-level completeness are unknown.

Verification and selection. After interaction, a unique manually crafted task evaluator checks final state against static ground truth or dynamically retrieved real-time truth. Only this post-execution check supplies the binary terminal outcome; no step reward is disclosed. The paper evaluates all attempted episodes rather than selecting trajectories for training. The later Hugging Face card describes full success and failure trajectories rather than success-only filtering, but raw gated archives were not inspected, so corrupt-run handling, omissions, and exact per-episode completeness remain unknown.

Evaluation use and release boundary. In the paper protocol, 17 models each run all 108 tasks three times. Toolathlon-Verified, released on 2026-06-30 after substantial changes to prompts, ground truths, evaluators, and infrastructure, packages three 108-task runs for each of 10 newer models, nominally 3,240 task-run episodes. Its current defaults include a 5,400-second task timeout and 64K maximum output length per agent turn; temperature and top-p inherit provider defaults. The official dataset policy permits benchmark evaluation, reproducibility, auditing, error analysis, and contamination research, and explicitly forbids pretraining, continued pretraining, SFT, preference/RL post-training, distillation, synthetic training-data generation, and benchmark-answering retrieval.

Reproduction must separately pin arXiv v2, ICLR/OpenReview metadata, repository commit 3b647e6, the task container image, dependencies, credentials and reset procedures, remote-service versions, each task/evaluator revision, provider endpoints/defaults, and Hugging Face revision 01deb377e5179d654e4282f62c0c336539480837. No single immutable manifest binds those components, and the repository has no Toolathlon-Verified tag or GitHub Release.

输入与任务构建。 研究人员和高年级计算机专业本科生先从 50 多个候选应用中自由寻找需求，再有针对性地补充重要但覆盖不足的应用。他们把这些需求改写为简洁、模糊的任务，使预期行为需要从环境、示例、文档或模板中推断。经过数周检查、过滤和细化，最终任务池包含 108 个任务。论文报告每个任务平均需要研究生投入 4–6 小时实现；随后由 5–6 名有经验的作者审核和修改，每轮检查每个任务约投入 5 小时，最后再做全 benchmark 交叉检查和 bug 修复（论文第 3.1–3.2 节，第 5–7 页）。拒绝数量、逐任务来源 URL、贡献者身份、reviewer agreement、裁决记录与 acceptance threshold 均为 unknown。

可执行任务 bundle。 一个已发布任务目录可能包含英文或中文 task/系统级指令、task_config.json、preprocess script 或 initial workspace、ground-truth workspace/state，以及 evaluation/main.py。配置为每个任务选择少于 10 个相关 MCP server，但会加载每个选中 server 暴露的全部工具；配置的本地工具可能包括 Python execution、web search、claim_done、sleep、超长输出导航和 context-history management。论文快照共包含 32 个 MCP server/application 表面、604 个 MCP 工具和 16 个本地工具；72 个任务具有显式状态初始化（论文表 2，第 6 页；第 2.4 节；官方仓库 tasks/finalpool/）。

交互与生成。 轨迹由被评测模型而非 teacher 生成：模型通过消息和工具调用，与远程服务及本地容器化软件交替交互。论文实验使用 OpenAI Agents SDK v0.0.15，处理 tool error，将超过 100K 字符的工具输出截断并以 10K 字符分页，还使用 context-history management；每个任务最多 100 turns（论文第 2.2 节与附录 B，第 14–15 页）。当前仓库另有 containerized/decoupled host loop 和初步 Claude Agent SDK 集成，不能把这些后续功能反投射到论文设置。论文没有披露跨 provider 统一的 temperature 或归一化 token/compute budget。

日志与输出。 在当前仓库 commit 3b647e60713703d653584c23ff185e3b6cd67722，主要 episode 日志是 traj_log.json，不是 JSONL。它保存 resolved task config、request/session ID、开始与完成时间、tool catalog/choice、执行状态、含 assistant tool_calls 和工具响应的消息历史、交互/工具调用次数、token 统计、成本、resume metadata 与 history path。evaluator 写出 eval_res.json，包含 pass=true/false/null 以及 detail 或 failure；eval_stats.json 聚合 run-level success 与 turn statistics。论文时期字段是否完全一致以及原始 archive 是否逐 episode 完整，均为 unknown。

验证与选择。 交互结束后，每个任务的人工定制 evaluator 把终态与静态 ground truth 或动态获取的实时 truth 比较。只有这个 post-execution check 提供 binary terminal outcome；论文未披露 step reward。论文评测所有尝试的 episode，并未为了训练而筛选轨迹。后续 Hugging Face card 将其描述为包含成功与失败的完整轨迹，而非只保留成功样本；但原始 gated archive 未被检查，因此 corrupt-run 处理、遗漏情况与逐 episode 完整性仍为 unknown。

评测用途与发布边界。 论文 protocol 中，17 个模型各自对全部 108 个任务运行 3 次。Toolathlon-Verified 于 2026-06-30 发布，其 prompt、ground truth、evaluator 与 infrastructure 已有实质修改；该发布为 10 个较新模型各打包 3 次完整 108-task 运行，名义上共有 3,240 个 task-run episode。当前默认值包括每个任务 5,400 秒 timeout，以及每次 agent turn 最多 64K 输出；temperature 与 top-p 继承 provider 默认值。官方 dataset policy 仅允许 benchmark evaluation、reproducibility、auditing、error analysis 与 contamination research，并明确禁止 pretraining、continued pretraining、SFT、preference/RL post-training、distillation、synthetic training-data generation 和用于回答 benchmark 的 retrieval。

复现必须分别固定 arXiv v2、ICLR/OpenReview metadata、仓库 commit 3b647e6、task container image、dependency、credential 与 reset procedure、remote-service 版本、每个 task/evaluator revision、provider endpoint/default，以及 Hugging Face revision 01deb377e5179d654e4282f62c0c336539480837。当前没有一个不可变 manifest 绑定这些组件，仓库也没有 Toolathlon-Verified tag 或 GitHub Release。

title: Evidence
证据
html:
Under the paper protocol, 17 models are run three times on all 108 tasks with at most 100 turns, yielding 5,508 task-run attempts by arithmetic from the disclosed design. The reported metrics are mean Pass@1 with standard deviation, Pass@3, Pass^3, and average turns. Table 3 reports Claude-4.5-Sonnet at 38.6% mean Pass@1 and DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp at 20.1%; these are paper-snapshot results, not current Toolathlon-Verified leaderboard values (Paper §4.1 and Table 3, pp. 7–8).

The score level is evidence that the 108 tasks are difficult for the tested systems under this scaffold, not proof that every task, evaluator, or recorded trajectory is high quality. A task can fail because of model planning, tool invocation, context handling, credentials, initialization, mutable external services, or the evaluator itself. Conversely, a deterministic terminal checker can pass an unintended route if its predicate omits a material side effect. The paper reports no task-level false-positive/false-negative study or adversarial evaluator audit.

The paper's failure analysis identifies tool-call errors, long-context degradation, premature stopping, and overlong tool outputs. Depending on the model, roughly 15%–35% of trajectories encounter overlong outputs; the OpenAI Agents SDK scaffold truncates outputs above 100K characters and provides 10K-character paging. This is a concrete interaction between benchmark infrastructure and measured agent behavior, but the observed association does not isolate a causal effect (Paper §5.1–§5.2, pp. 8–9; Appendix B, pp. 14–15).

The later release provides a different evidence surface. Toolathlon-Verified is dated 2026-06-30 and states that prompts, ground truths, evaluators, and infrastructure were substantially revised. Its gated Hugging Face card lists 10 model archives with three complete 108-task runs each; 30 run summaries cover all 108 tasks, nominally 3,240 episodes. It also warns that some summary.config_used model labels are stale and some models have fewer than 324 valid AvgTurns records. These warnings support auditability, but the inaccessible raw archives prevent independent confirmation of file-level completeness, redaction changes, and corrupt or dropped episode handling.

Paper and current-release scores must not be merged into a single progress curve. The benchmark artifacts, evaluator behavior, infrastructure, provider defaults, and model generations changed, and no immutable manifest maps the paper snapshot to repository commit 3b647e6 and Hugging Face revision 01deb37. All numerical results remain author-reported and not independently reproduced in the checked evidence. They establish comparative performance under specified snapshots; they do not establish contamination freedom, trajectory training value, reusable licensing, or stationary benchmark validity.

在论文 protocol 下，17 个模型各自对 108 个任务运行 3 次，每次最多 100 turns；根据已披露设计计算，共有 5,508 个 task-run attempt。报告指标包括带标准差的 mean Pass@1、Pass@3、Pass^3 与 average turns。表 3 报告 Claude-4.5-Sonnet 的 mean Pass@1 为 38.6%，DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp 为 20.1%；这些是论文快照结果，不是当前 Toolathlon-Verified leaderboard 数值（论文第 4.1 节与表 3，第 7–8 页）。

这些分数表明，在该 scaffold 下，108 个任务对被测系统具有难度；它们不能证明每个任务、evaluator 或记录轨迹都具有高质量。任务失败可能来自模型规划、工具调用、context handling、credential、初始化、可变外部服务或 evaluator 本身。反过来，如果 terminal checker 的谓词遗漏重要副作用，确定性 evaluator 也可能放过非预期路径。论文没有报告逐任务 false-positive/false-negative 研究或对抗性 evaluator 审计。

论文 failure analysis 指出 tool-call error、long-context degradation、premature stopping 与 overlong tool output。不同模型约有 15%–35% 的轨迹遇到超长输出；OpenAI Agents SDK scaffold 会截断超过 100K 字符的输出，并提供 10K 字符分页。这具体展示了 benchmark infrastructure 与被测智能体行为之间的耦合，但所观察到的关联没有隔离出因果效应（论文第 5.1–5.2 节，第 8–9 页；附录 B，第 14–15 页）。

后续发布提供了不同的 evidence surface。Toolathlon-Verified 发布于 2026-06-30，并说明 prompt、ground truth、evaluator 与 infrastructure 已被实质修改。其 gated Hugging Face card 列出 10 个模型 archive，每个含 3 次完整 108-task 运行；30 份 run summary 均覆盖 108 个任务，名义上共 3,240 个 episode。发布还警告部分 summary.config_used 模型标签过时，且某些模型少于 324 条有效 AvgTurns 记录。这些警告有助于审计，但原始 archive 无法访问，因此不能独立确认文件级完整性、redaction 变化，以及 corrupt 或 dropped episode 的处理。

不能把论文分数与当前 release 分数合并为一条进展曲线。benchmark artifact、evaluator 行为、infrastructure、provider 默认值与模型生成均已变化，而且没有不可变 manifest 把论文快照映射到仓库 commit 3b647e6 和 Hugging Face revision 01deb37。所有数值结果均为作者报告，未在已检查证据中得到独立复现。它们证明的是指定快照下的相对表现，不能证明无污染、轨迹具有训练价值、许可证允许复用，或 benchmark 始终有效。

title: Novelty
新意
html:
Prior language-agent benchmarks already evaluate tool use, application interaction, or multi-step work; deterministic execution checks are also not inherently new. Toolathlon changes the evaluation object by combining a deliberately fuzzy user request, a large but task-restricted MCP/local-tool surface, initialized cross-application state, a long state-action-tool episode, and one manually written final-state evaluator for each of 108 tasks. This is more specific than reporting tool-call correctness in isolation because both environment mutation and the terminal predicate become part of the record.

The construction design also changes what task quality means. Tasks are drawn from real-world websites or crafted to reflect genuine demands, then refined over multiple weeks and checked by 5–6 experienced authors. The resulting prompt often omits intermediate subgoals, requiring an agent to infer them from examples, documents, templates, and current environment state. That provides a concrete surface for long-horizon planning and recovery, while the paper's broad 32-surface, 604-MCP-tool integration is partly an engineering-scale contribution rather than a new learning algorithm (Paper §§2–3 and Table 2).

For reasoning-data research, the direction signal is the explicit separation between trajectory richness and supervision richness. Toolathlon logs detailed state-action events, but attaches only a deterministic binary outcome to the completed episode. This makes it possible to audit where an agent acted, what it observed, how the environment changed, and whether the terminal predicate passed without pretending that intermediate actions have verified labels.

What is not introduced should remain visible. The work does not propose a new optimizer, base-model training method, teacher policy, step-level reward model, preference signal, or process-supervision scheme. It evaluates multiple existing agents. The current repository's additional host loops and Claude Agent SDK support, and the 2026 Toolathlon-Verified task/evaluator revisions, are later artifact evolution rather than paper-era novelty.

Neither scale nor benchmark score is a quality certificate. The 108 tasks have substantial manual review, but rejected-task counts, reviewer agreement, acceptance thresholds, per-task source provenance, evaluator error rates, and a record-level change ledger are unknown. Before reuse, researchers must inspect task/evaluator revisions, confirm archive completeness and redaction, pin the environment stack, and respect the official prohibition on training. The novelty supports evaluation and audit design; it does not justify converting the trajectories into post-training data.

既有语言智能体 benchmark 已经评测工具使用、应用交互或多步工作；确定性 execution check 本身也不是新机制。Toolathlon 改变的是评测对象的组合方式：把刻意保持模糊的用户请求、大规模但按任务收窄的 MCP/本地工具面、初始化跨应用状态、长程 state-action-tool episode，以及 108 个任务各自的人工终态 evaluator 结合起来。相较孤立报告工具调用正确率，这一对象更具体，因为环境修改与 terminal predicate 都成为记录的一部分。

构建设计也改变了任务质量的含义。任务来自真实网站需求，或由作者构造以反映真实需求，随后经过数周细化，并由 5–6 名有经验的作者检查。最终 prompt 经常省略中间子目标，要求智能体从示例、文档、模板和当前环境状态中推断。这提供了具体的长程规划与恢复评测面；同时，论文整合 32 个环境表面和 604 个 MCP 工具，其中一部分贡献属于工程规模扩展，而不是新的学习算法（论文第 2–3 节与表 2）。

对 reasoning data 研究而言，方向信号是明确区分轨迹丰富度与监督丰富度。Toolathlon 记录详细 state-action 事件，但只在完整 episode 上附着确定性 binary outcome。研究者因此可以审计智能体在哪里行动、观察到什么、环境如何变化，以及 terminal predicate 是否通过，同时不把中间动作伪装成已验证标签。

哪些内容不是新贡献也应保持清楚。该工作没有提出新 optimizer、base-model 训练方法、teacher policy、step-level reward model、preference signal 或 process-supervision scheme，而是评测多个既有智能体。当前仓库增加的 host loop 与 Claude Agent SDK 支持，以及 2026 年 Toolathlon-Verified 的 task/evaluator 修订，都属于后续 artifact 演化，不是论文时期的新意。

规模和 benchmark 分数都不是质量认证。108 个任务经过大量人工检查，但 rejected-task 数量、reviewer agreement、acceptance threshold、逐任务来源 provenance、evaluator 错误率与逐记录变更 ledger 均为 unknown。复用前，研究者必须检查 task/evaluator revision，确认 archive 完整性与 redaction，固定环境栈，并遵守官方训练禁令。该新意支持评测与审计设计，不能作为把轨迹转换成后训练数据的依据。

title: Limitations
局限
html:
• Terminal-verifier risk: a deterministic script is reproducible only for the state fields and service responses it actually queries. Missing predicates can create false positives, overly strict snapshots can create false negatives, and public evaluator code can invite verifier gaming. No task-level error rate, adversarial test, or independent evaluator audit is reported; this is a curator risk inference from the feedback contract.
  • Dynamic-environment risk: some ground truth is retrieved in real time, and the task substrate mixes mutable remote services, accounts, APIs, credentials, and local containers. An unchanged agent can receive a different score after data, permissions, service behavior, or availability changes. claim_done or normal loop termination does not protect against this brittleness because correctness is checked afterward.
  • Version-drift risk: Toolathlon-Verified on 2026-06-30 substantially revised prompts, ground truths, evaluators, and infrastructure relative to the paper. The checked repository commit is 3b647e6 and the checked Hugging Face revision is 01deb37, but there is no repository tag, GitHub Release, or immutable manifest tying paper version, code, container image, external services, evaluators, and archives together. Paper and current leaderboard scores are therefore not directly comparable.
  • Contamination and split risk: one public 108-task pool is reused across every released run; no train/dev/test split, hidden test set, public/private partition, systematic near-duplicate audit, or benchmark-overlap study is disclosed. Prompts, ground truths, evaluator code, and trajectories expose direct contamination and evaluator-gaming surfaces. A canary plus DECONTAMINATION.md and decontamination.json exist, but the detailed files are gated and were not inspected.
  • Release, rights, and privacy risk: raw trajectory archives are gated, so exact episode inventory, hashes, redaction diffs, omitted/corrupt-run policy, and file-level completeness are unknown. The paper is CC BY 4.0, but no general-purpose license was verified for repository code, task assets, ground truths, environment snapshots, trajectories, or third-party application content. The release reports credential/endpoint sanitization, yet independent redaction recall, consent, and third-party-content rights remain unknown.
  • Construction and reproducibility risk: per-task source URLs, contributor attribution, rejected-task counts, reviewer decisions, agreement, and acceptance thresholds are undisclosed. Provider temperature and top-p inherit upstream defaults in the current release; model endpoints, total token/compute budgets, reset procedures, and external-service versions are not normalized or immutably pinned. The paper's observed tool-call errors, long-context degradation, premature stopping, and 15%–35% overlong-output incidence can therefore reflect both agent behavior and scaffold/environment choices.

• 终态 verifier 风险： 确定性脚本只能对其实际查询的状态字段与服务响应实现可复现检查。谓词遗漏可能产生 false positive，过严快照可能产生 false negative，公开 evaluator code 还可能诱发 verifier gaming。论文没有报告逐任务错误率、对抗测试或独立 evaluator 审计；这是依据反馈契约得到的 curator risk inference。
  • 动态环境风险： 部分 ground truth 实时获取，任务 substrate 又混合可变的远程服务、账号、API、credential 与本地容器。即使智能体不变，数据、权限、服务行为或可用性改变后，分数也可能变化。claim_done 或正常 loop termination 不能消除这种脆弱性，因为正确性在其后才被检查。
  • 版本漂移风险： 2026-06-30 的 Toolathlon-Verified 相对论文实质修改了 prompt、ground truth、evaluator 与 infrastructure。已检查仓库 commit 为 3b647e6，Hugging Face revision 为 01deb37，但没有 repository tag、GitHub Release 或不可变 manifest 把论文版本、代码、container image、外部服务、evaluator 与 archive 绑定起来。因此，论文分数与当前 leaderboard 分数不可直接比较。
  • 污染与划分风险： 一个公开的 108-task pool 被每次发布运行重复使用；论文未披露 train/dev/test split、hidden test set、public/private partition、系统化近重复审计或 benchmark overlap 研究。prompt、ground truth、evaluator code 与轨迹形成直接污染和 evaluator gaming 表面。发布包含 canary，并指向 DECONTAMINATION.md 与 decontamination.json，但详细文件受 gated access 限制，未被检查。
  • 发布、权利与隐私风险： 原始轨迹 archive 受 gated access 限制，因此精确 episode inventory、hash、redaction diff、omitted/corrupt-run policy 与文件级完整性均为 unknown。论文采用 CC BY 4.0，但仓库代码、任务资产、ground truth、环境快照、轨迹及第三方应用内容均未核验到通用许可证。发布声明已清理 credential/endpoint，但独立 redaction recall、consent 与第三方内容权利仍为 unknown。
  • 构建与复现风险： 逐任务来源 URL、贡献者归属、rejected-task 数量、reviewer decision、agreement 与 acceptance threshold 均未披露。当前发布的 provider temperature 与 top-p 继承上游默认值；model endpoint、总 token/compute budget、reset procedure 和外部服务版本没有归一化或不可变固定。论文观察到的 tool-call error、long-context degradation、premature stopping 与 15%–35% overlong-output incidence 因此可能同时反映智能体行为以及 scaffold/environment 选择。

title: Usefulness
用途
html:
For the assigned environment_agent_trajectory_data track, Toolathlon is a concrete evaluation and audit object for studying how a fuzzy task becomes an executable episode. Researchers can preserve the task prompt, initial state, selected tool surface, ordered assistant/tool messages, observations, execution status, terminal evaluator output, timing, token use, and cost, then analyze planning failures, recovery behavior, tool errors, context pressure, premature stopping, and environment-induced failures without collapsing the episode into a final answer.

For benchmarks_evaluation_surfaces, the task-specific evaluator design is useful as both a baseline and an audit target. A replication can compare the published deterministic final-state predicate with stricter state invariants, alternate-valid-state tests, perturbation/adversarial cases, delayed-side-effect checks, and manual review. It should separately report execution failure, evaluator false, and evaluator null rather than mapping all outcomes into an undifferentiated zero.

The paper/release boundary also supplies a practical version-drift experiment. Researchers can replay the same model against the paper-like snapshot and Toolathlon-Verified, attribute changes to prompt, ground-truth, evaluator, infrastructure, or provider revisions, and quantify how benchmark maintenance alters measured capability. Such work requires a manifest with task/evaluator hashes, container and dependency identifiers, service timestamps, reset state, model endpoint and decoding defaults, and archive revision.

The 30 released run summaries and nominal 3,240 Toolathlon-Verified episodes can support leaderboard reproducibility checks, error taxonomies, cost/turn analysis, redaction audits, and contamination detection after authorized access. Because raw archives are gated, file-level completeness and sanitization must be checked before making claims about the release. Reported benchmark performance alone is not evidence of trajectory quality.

Reuse class: evaluation and audit only. The official release explicitly forbids all training, distillation, synthetic-data generation, and benchmark-answering retrieval uses, while general-purpose licenses for code, task assets, environment snapshots, and trajectories are unresolved. Do not use these episodes for SFT, RLVR, preference optimization, process-reward training, or pretraining, even if their state-action structure is technically convertible.

对指定的 environment_agent_trajectory_data 方向而言，Toolathlon 是研究“模糊任务如何转化为可执行 episode”的具体评测与审计对象。研究者可以保留 task prompt、initial state、选定工具面、有序 assistant/tool message、observation、执行状态、终态 evaluator output、时间、token 使用与成本，再分析规划失败、恢复行为、工具错误、context 压力、premature stopping 与环境导致的失败，而不是把 episode 压缩成最终答案。

对 benchmarks_evaluation_surfaces 而言，任务专属 evaluator 既可作为 baseline，也可作为审计对象。复现实验可以把已发布的确定性 final-state predicate，与更严格的 state invariant、alternate-valid-state test、扰动/对抗 case、延迟副作用检查和人工复核比较。应分别报告 execution failure、evaluator false 与 evaluator null，不能把所有结果都映射成不可区分的零分。

论文与 release 的边界还提供了可执行的版本漂移实验。研究者可以让同一模型分别运行在接近论文的快照与 Toolathlon-Verified 上，把变化归因到 prompt、ground truth、evaluator、infrastructure 或 provider revision，并量化 benchmark 维护如何改变所测能力。这类研究需要 manifest 记录 task/evaluator hash、container/dependency identifier、service timestamp、reset state、model endpoint 与 decoding default，以及 archive revision。

在获得授权访问后，30 份已发布 run summary 与名义上的 3,240 个 Toolathlon-Verified episode 可用于 leaderboard reproducibility check、错误分类、成本/turn 分析、redaction 审计与污染检测。由于原始 archive 受 gated access 限制，在对发布完整性作出主张前必须先检查文件级完整性与 sanitization。仅有 benchmark 性能不能作为轨迹质量证据。

复用等级：仅限 evaluation 与 audit。官方发布明确禁止所有训练、distillation、synthetic-data generation 与用于回答 benchmark 的 retrieval；代码、任务资产、环境快照与轨迹的通用许可证也未解决。即使这些 episode 的 state-action 结构在技术上可转换，也不得用于 SFT、RLVR、preference optimization、process-reward training 或 pretraining。

title: Reading notes
阅读笔记
html:
• Start with Paper §§2–3 and Table 2: the object is 108 executable fuzzy tasks over 32 MCP-server/application surfaces and 604 MCP tools, not a static prompt set.
  • Keep the supervision boundary explicit: logs contain state-action-tool events, but correctness is one deterministic terminal pass; no step-level reward or process label is disclosed.
  • Read Paper Table 3 and §5 together: 38.6% is the paper-snapshot top mean Pass@1, while 15%–35% overlong-output incidence shows scaffold behavior is part of the measurement.
  • Treat Toolathlon-Verified (2026-06-30) as a materially revised release, not a silent replacement for the paper; pin repo 3b647e6 and HF 01deb37 when auditing current artifacts.
  • Read alongside MCP-AgentBench, τ2-bench, and TheAgentCompany to compare MCP breadth, stateful interaction, and long-horizon multi-application evaluation contracts.
  • Before reuse, resolve licensing, inspect the gated archives and decontamination files, test evaluator false positives/negatives, and obey the official do-not-train policy.

• 先读论文第 2–3 节与表 2：数据对象是覆盖 32 个 MCP server/application 表面和 604 个 MCP 工具的 108 个可执行模糊任务，不是静态 prompt 集合。
  • 必须明确监督边界：日志包含 state-action-tool 事件，但正确性只是一个确定性终态 pass；论文未披露 step-level reward 或 process label。
  • 应把论文表 3 与第 5 节一起读：38.6% 是论文快照最高 mean Pass@1，而 15%–35% overlong-output incidence 表明 scaffold 行为也是测量的一部分。
  • 应把 Toolathlon-Verified（2026-06-30）视为实质修订的 release，而不是论文的静默替代；审计当前 artifact 时固定 repo 3b647e6 与 HF 01deb37。
  • 建议与 MCP-AgentBench、τ2-bench 和 TheAgentCompany 对读，以比较 MCP 工具广度、有状态交互与长程多应用评测契约。
  • 复用前应解决许可证，检查 gated archive 与 decontamination 文件，测试 evaluator false positive/negative，并遵守官方 do-not-train policy。

value.html: A pool of 108 concise, fuzzy long-horizon tasks manually sourced from real-world websites or crafted by the authors to reflect genuine user demands. The authors first sourced freely from more than 50 candidate applications, then targeted important underrepresented applications.

Sequential tool/environment responses and workspace/application state exposed through MCP and local tools. The paper mixes remote services with locally containerized applications; 72 of 108 tasks have scripted and/or workspace-based state initialization.

Tool calls over the task's configured set of fewer than 10 relevant MCP servers, with every tool in each selected server loaded, plus configured local tools such as Python execution, web search, claim_done, sleep, overlong-output navigation, and context-history management. Paper Table 2 reports 604 MCP tools and 16 local tools overall.

An executable task bundle plus an episode log. A task bundle may include English/Chinese task and system-level instructions, task_config.json, preprocess or initial-workspace assets, ground-truth workspace/state, and a task-specific evaluator. Current traj_log.json records config, request/timestamps, tool catalog and choice, execution status, message history, key statistics, costs, resume/session metadata; eval_res.json records pass/details/failure.

The language agent/model under evaluation produces the episode. Paper experiments evaluate 17 models with three runs per task; the later Toolathlon-Verified trajectory release packages three complete 108-task runs for each of 10 newer models.

Thirty-two MCP-server/application surfaces spanning remote services and locally containerized Poste.io, Canvas, Kubernetes, WooCommerce, and other software; task execution is isolated in containers. Current reproduction additionally depends on Docker/Podman, account credentials, external services, repository code, and a task container image.

A unique manually written deterministic evaluator for each task compares the final workspace/application state with a static ground-truth snapshot or dynamically retrieved real-time ground truth. Current TaskEvaluator returns binary pass/fail only after successful execution and uses null pass when execution status is not SUCCESS.
eval_res.json with pass=true/false/null plus details or failure; run-level eval_stats.json aggregates success and turn statistics.
Terminal binary task success. No step-level reward, critique, preference, or process label is disclosed.

The episode is successful only when the task-specific post-execution evaluator passes against the resulting state. Agent-loop termination, a final natural-language response, or claim_done alone does not establish correctness.

Real-world need or author-crafted need -> two-stage application-aware task sourcing -> multi-week filtering/refinement -> task prompt/config/state initializer/ground truth/evaluator -> isolated model-environment interaction -> traj_log.json and eval_res.json -> three-run summaries and gated Toolathlon-Verified model archives. Record-level source and contributor identities are unknown.
Not applicable as one training recipe: Toolathlon evaluates multiple proprietary and open-weight agents and does not train a base model.
No teacher supplies target trajectories. Authors manually construct tasks, environment states, ground truth, and evaluators.
The evaluated agent/model generates tool-use trajectories in the released environment.

Authors/researchers and senior CS undergraduates source tasks from real-world websites or craft them to match genuine user needs; exact source URL and author provenance per task are generally undisclosed.

Paper: each of 17 models is run three times on all 108 tasks with at most 100 turns. Toolathlon-Verified trajectory release: 10 model archives, three runs per model, every run covering the same 108 tasks, nominally 3,240 task-run episodes.
Three runs per model-task for both the paper evaluation protocol and the current Toolathlon-Verified archives.
Paper setting unknown. Current Toolathlon-Verified README says temperature and top-p are not set by the framework and inherit upstream provider defaults.

Paper uses OpenAI Agents SDK v0.0.15 with tool-error handling, 100K-character overlong-output truncation plus 10K-character paging, and context-history management. Current repository also offers containerized and decoupled host loops and preliminary Claude Agent SDK support.
unknown

Tasks undergo multiple weeks of checking, filtering, and refinement, followed by review/revision by 5-6 experienced authors and benchmark-wide cross-checking. Toolathlon-Verified states that prompts, ground truths, and evaluators were reviewed and aligned. Rejected task counts, adjudication logs, and exact acceptance thresholds are unknown.

Paper experiments allow at most 100 turns. Current Toolathlon-Verified allows 5,400 seconds per task and 64K maximum output length per agent turn; total token/compute budgets vary by model and are not normalized.
Evaluation scaffold only; no optimizer or post-training objective is part of the paper.

Manually sourced or crafted tasks across research, campus, finance, technology, business, daily-life, and e-commerce workflows; environments combine remote real services, locally containerized software, files, and dynamically changing external information.
One public 108-task evaluation pool is described and released. No train/dev/test split, hidden test set, or public/private partition is disclosed; every released model run covers the same 108 tasks.
No systematic overlap or near-duplicate audit against other agent benchmarks, training corpora, or public workflow templates is disclosed.

The gated trajectory release includes a canary GUID and points to DECONTAMINATION.md and decontamination.json, but their detailed contents could not be inspected without access approval. The dataset explicitly prohibits training and benchmark-answering retrieval; public task prompts, ground truths, and evaluators still create a direct contamination surface.

The HF card calls the release full trajectories, states that all 30 run summaries cover all 108 tasks, and reports both success and failure outcomes, so it is not described as success-filtered. Exact archive-level episode completeness, corrupt-run handling, and any omitted trajectories remain unknown because access is gated.

items: Evaluator and ground-truth drift is material: Toolathlon-Verified substantially revised task prompts, ground truths, evaluators, and infrastructure after the paper, and repository review logs document later task-specific fixes.
Dynamic evaluators depend on mutable external information and services; environment/account/API changes can alter task solvability or scoring even when agent behavior is unchanged.

Public prompts, ground truths, evaluator code, and released trajectories create benchmark contamination and evaluator-gaming risk; the official data policy therefore forbids training and benchmark-answering retrieval.
A deterministic terminal script can still have task-specific false positives or false negatives; the paper does not report evaluator error rates or adversarial robustness.
Tool availability, credentials, reset procedures, container images, SDK/scaffold behavior, provider defaults, and external-service versions are not tied together in one immutable replay manifest.

The paper identifies tool-call errors, long-context degradation, premature stopping, and overlong tool outputs; 15%-35% of model trajectories encounter overlong outputs, and framework truncation/context management can affect measured capability.
Current trajectory summaries warn that summary.config_used may contain stale model labels and that some model runs have fewer than 324 valid AvgTurns records.
Repository/task/data licensing is unresolved, and the gated archive's benchmark-only policy blocks training reuse even if the raw record format is technically convertible.
Paper scores and current Toolathlon-Verified leaderboard scores are not directly comparable because both benchmark artifacts and evaluated model generations changed.

value.html: Paper Appendix E removes personally identifiable information from displayed examples. The HF release says archives were scanned and sanitized for API credentials, endpoints/base URLs, high-confidence credential patterns, and credential-bearing signed URLs, while warning downstream users to review derived subsets. Independent redaction recall, consent, and third-party-content rights are unknown.

The arXiv paper is CC BY 4.0. At repository commit 3b647e60713703d653584c23ff185e3b6cd67722, GitHub reports no SPDX license and the tree has no root LICENSE. The gated HF benchmark-only access policy is not a verified reusable license for trajectories, task assets, ground truths, or third-party application content.

Task need -> prompt/config -> initial state and ground truth -> deterministic task evaluator -> evaluated model's user/assistant/tool message episode -> execution status and binary evaluator result -> per-run eval_stats -> gated model archive. The release lacks one immutable manifest tying paper version, code commit, container image, service versions, task/evaluator revisions, and archive revision together.

Paper arXiv v2 (2026-02-26); Toolathlon-Verified named release (2026-06-30); repository main checked at 3b647e60713703d653584c23ff185e3b6cd67722 (2026-07-15); HF dataset checked at 01deb377e5179d654e4282f62c0c336539480837 (2026-07-16). The GitHub repository has no tag or GitHub Release for Toolathlon-Verified.
